title: The Dental X-Ray
narration: My dentist found a tracking device inside my jaw. The capsule matched X-rays from six patients who disappeared after visiting our childhood clinic. When its light blinked, two men entered and dragged the dentist away while I hid in a cupboard. A caller thanked me for locating their defective tracker, lost twenty years earlier. The cupboard light switched on. The silence felt deliberate, as though someone nearby was waiting for me to understand the trap before moving again. For several seconds I could hear nothing except my breathing and the small ordinary sounds around me. Every explanation I tried made the details worse, because each clue had been placed where I alone would find it. Its walls were covered with childhood photographs of me sleeping—and the dentist had taken every one.
